A resurfaced Hunger Games deleted scene proves the Capitol wanted the games to last forever, as Quarter Quells were planned centuries in advance

When you purchase through links on our site, we may earn an affiliate commission. Here’s how it works.

13 years later, a deleted scene from The Hunger Games: Catching Fire has resurfaced online, but a closer look at the background unveils a chilling secret about what the Capitol had planned for the future of the games.

In the deleted scene, which you can watch on YouTube, gamemeeper Plutarch (Philip Seymour Hoffman) goes to the Capitol Vault to find out what 'twist' will take place in the third Quarter Quell. However, we see him burn the paper that was in the third Quarter Quell safe and replace it with a new card. But that's not the most interesting part, as in the wide shot, we see that there are at least 70 safes in the vault. This means the Capitol has planned for centuries' worth of Quarter Quells.

"That wall of envelopes wasn't just about the 75th Games," said one fan on Twitter. "It showed the Capitol had already written rules for future Quarter Quells, meaning they planned for the Hunger Games to continue for another 2,000 years. The districts were never supposed to get free. The 'tradition' was always a lie designed to last forever."

It isn't too surprising that the Capitol would want the Hunger Games to last forever. The whole system was set up to benefit the rich after the poor rebelled, plummeting the nation into what is known as 'The Dark Days'. The games quench the nation's thirst for blood while keeping the districts in check. However, it is rather chilling to think that those who set up the games planned on having children kill one another for centuries to come, even thinking of sick twists every 25 years.

In the world of The Hunger Games, every 25 years, the Capitol marks the anniversary by including a twist to keep the games exciting. The first Quarter Quell, mentioned in author Suzanne Collins' works, forced each district to elect its own tributes rather than using the lottery reaping process. The second Quarter Quell, which we will see play out in new prequel movie The Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping, sent in double the number of tributes than ever before.

The third Quarter Quell only reaped winning victors from each district, sending Katniss and Peeta back into the arena just one year after they had won. Of course, in the sequel we find out that Plutarch planted this twist on purpose, so he could keep Katniss safe in the arena while the rebellion brewed outside. When the time was right, he plucked Katniss from the games and took her to District 13 in The Mockingjay Part 1.

Plutarch, this time played by Jesse Plemons, will return in Sunrise on the Reaping, which hits theaters on November 20. For more, keep up with other upcoming movies with our list of movie release dates still to come.

#3934. Xbox boss announces Wolfenstein 3 and confirms new game in development at idSoftware despite reported job cut "bloodbath"

"One of gaming's most important franchises".

Xbox boss Asha Sharma has confirmed Wolfenstein 3 is in development at MachineGames, the Swedish studio behind the acclaimed Wolfenstein: The New Order, Wolfenstein 2: The New Colossal, and 2024's celebrated Indiana Jones and the Great Circle. Additionally, she revealed Doom developer idSoftware - one of the Microsoft-owned studios heavily impacted by sweeping Xbox job cuts earlier this year - is now working on a new game.

Sharma has, of course, been on a bit of a PR offensive of late, positioning herself alongside snippets of positive news at a time Xbox is embroiled in a massive business "reset" effort that has resulted in proposed studio closures and mass layoffs that will ultimately see 3,200 Xbox employees lose their jobs. This week's Wolfenstein 3 reveal similarly arrived in the form of a tweet posted directly from her social media account.

"Wolfenstein 3 is officially in production at MachineGames," Sharma wrote on X. "One of gaming's most important franchises, and a team that has done remarkable work bringing it forward. Looking forward to sharing more." As for idSoftware's new project, confirmation of that - again attributed directly to Sharma - appeared in a post on Bethesda's website. "Slaughter Mode comes to Doom: The Dark Ages - Revelations on Monday," she wrote, "and the team is already working on its next game."

In July, sweeping job cuts at Xbox resulted in 96 of idSoftware's 136 employees being laid off in a move one former team member described as a "bloodbath". Since then, idSoftware co-studio director Marty Stratton has attempted to downplay the cuts, recently insisting the studio was "doing great". He added id was "working more closely than ever" with MachineGames - a studio which appears to have escaped Sharma's restructuring efforts so far.

This week's Wolfenstein and idSoftware news follows similar efforts by Xbox to reassure fans their favourite franchises are unaffected by the recent layoffs. Shortly after substantial job cuts at Bethesda were confirmed, the company moved to insist The Elder Scrolls 6 was still "on the way" and that its plans were "unaffected" (the company has since released a trailer announcing its subtitle). It also confirmed a new Fallout game was in development.

Xbox's year of bad news - which includes ongoing boycott efforts relating to Microsoft's controversial involvement with the Israeli military - comes as the division celebrates its 25th anniversary. Earlier this week, Sharma shared a memo to staff marking the occasion, albeit one in which she seemingly championed a gen-AI future for games development, enthusing that, "A small team will be able to build worlds that today demand hundreds of developers".

#3933. Forage and fight for ingredients in a magical 1960s Italy and whip up some tasty meals Cooking Mama style in The Snackbar at the End of the World

If a game is about cooking, at minimum I'll have to give it a quick testspin. Outside of this whole writing about video games thing, my other lot in life is soul bound to food, so I'm always curious to see how the two can be mixed together. And earlier this week, The Snackbar at the End of the World was revealed, a wonderfully cartoonish action-adventure game set in a magical, slightly post-apocalyptic version of 1960s Italy where you go out and forage for ingredients while fending off monstrous crops before turning them into tasty meals back in your struggling restaurant.

First up, I just have to gush over the artstyle a bit. The whole game is hand-drawn with a colourful, comic book look that has an impressive sense of depth to it. It gives off a deep love of Italian architecture and landscapes, and that admiration clearly extends to the food too. Once you've gotten the ingredients you need, you then, loosely in the vein of Cooking Mama, prepare them and make various classic Italian dishes by performing some quick minigames. Simple, but charming! The rest of the time you're off killing some ghoulies that look like mutated fruit and veggies, with the occasional fungus-possessed hog and, uh, haunted statues? I think?

I'm also quite pleased about two points made on the game's Steam page. First is the content description: "This game features cartoon violence, sensitive political themes set in a fictional world, and depictions of an oppressive government committing crimes against its citizens." There is clearly a romantic quality to the game and I'd be worried if it didn't acknowledge any of the political context of the decades preceding.

The other line reads, "Every sound effect, musical note, design decision, and line of code is human-made. Because this game is about human relationships and delicious food – and that’s not a story we would ever trust AI to tell." Thank the lord! Right now there's no release date attached to The Snackbar at the End of the World, unsurprising given it was only announced this week. But while we all wait for a date, you could perhaps join me in throwing it a wishlist on Steam.

#3932. GTA 6's Mandy 'Is a Lot of Fun' Says Real-Life Actress as PS5 Players Are Smitten

I knew when I was reviewing GTA 6 that bunny boiler Mandy was going to take social media by storm, and it was quite fun watching the web react to Chapter 1’s ‘Pipeworks’ mission as the game launched overnight.

Now it’s being played by millions, actress Lexie Shoaibi has revealed she stars as the character, who not-so subtly throws herself at Jason during a very early story mission.

I actually think this is one example of the game’s slightly more mature writing. Wait, don’t roll your eyes – just hear me out, okay?

While this whole quest is played more for laughs, it’s there to establish the strength of Jason and Lucia’s relationship, as Jason shows no signs of being tempted by Mandy’s advances.

“She’s a lot of fun,” Shoaibi said, after confirming she did voice acting and motion capture for the character. At the time of writing, her post on Instagram has received over 90k likes.

But the response on social media would suggest gamers think she’s more than a “lot of fun”.

One post by Complex, featuring a few images and the caption ‘Mandy from GTA 6’, attracted 37 million views in just a few hours. Pertinently, it’s been bookmarked 54k times.

I don’t want to analyse this character too deeply, but I think it’s the moment I realised Rockstar has really pushed the boat out here.

The sheer variety of body types, and the detail invested into them, is unprecedented really. Mandy is just one of many similarly realistic NPCs in the game.

And while the character is almost certainly a psychopath, it’s been amusing to see her go viral overnight.

Crimson Desert might have missed out on a Game of the Year nomination at The Game Awards, but it did just take home the big prize – along with seven others – at the Korea Game Awards.

Per Inven Global, in addition to taking home the Grand Prize and the Global Game Award, Crimson Desert won four technical categories: sound, graphics, character design, and planning/scenario. That's in addition to a Best Developer Award and protagonist Kliff's Korean voice actor, Lee Hyun, receiving the Popular Voice Actor award.

According to The Korea Herald, this is a record-breaking sweep for a game at the show. The previous best was six awards for a single game, a feat Lies of P and Lost Ark had both achieved.

Fans will be pleased that Crimson Desert is getting some recognition here, at least – many felt that the open-world behemoth had been snubbed at The Game Awards when nominations were announced earlier this week. In addition to missing out on a Game of the Year nomination, Crimson Desert has been nominated for only one category – Best Community Support.

Pocketpair publishing and communications lead John "Bucky" Buckley was one of the many fans disappointed about this – especially the fact that it missed out on the RPG and adventure game categories. "To say I'm disappointed would be an understatement," he said. "What a shame. What a terrible shame."

However, developer Pearl Abyss has shown nothing but gratitude for Crimson Desert's Best Community Support nomination. "This wouldn't have been possible without you, Greymanes," it writes on the official Crimson Desert account. "Thank you for supporting us on this journey, it truly means the world to us."

Despite Crimson Desert's AI backlash, Pearl Abyss is now implementing the tech "throughout our entire development pipeline" – including for upcoming Pokemon-like DokeV.

Weekly digests, tales from the communities you love, and more

I'm GamesRadar+'s Deputy News Editor, working alongside the rest of the news team to deliver cool gaming stories that we love. After spending more hours than I can count filling The University of Sheffield's student newspaper with Pokemon and indie game content, and picking up a degree in Journalism Studies, I started my career at GAMINGbible where I worked as a journalist for over a year and a half. I then became TechRadar Gaming's news writer, where I sourced stories and wrote about all sorts of intriguing topics. In my spare time, you're sure to find me on my Nintendo Switch or PS5 playing through story-driven RPGs like Xenoblade Chronicles and Persona 5 Royal, nuzlocking old Pokemon games, or going for a Victory Royale in Fortnite.

#3929. Slay the Spire 2 gets its first new character since its massively successful launch in March as part of "biggest" beta patch yet

A week dedicated to all things Grand Theft Auto, as the long-awaited GTA 6 finally arrives.

Slay the Spire 2, which released into early access earlier this year, is expanding once more with a major new beta update. This introduces the deckbuilder's first new character since launch - a whimsical musician armed with a bow - alongside two new modes, and more.

When Slay the Spire 2 arrived back in March, it was to much enthusiastic acclaim. Eurogamer's Bertie Purchie is a big fan, and has trumpeted its successes on multiple occasions, calling the sequel's co-op mode "transformative". And it was a commercial hit too, managing to shift over 5m copies in just a month of release. All of which means there are plenty of eyes on Slay the Spire 2, eager to see what developer MegaCrit does next.

So far major updates have brought the likes of buffs, balance adjustments, art updates, UI improvements, bug fixes, and more - and MegaCrit has also made other substantial adjustments including the jettisoning of third act boss Doormaker, after it decided the encounter was overly complex. And now, as 2026 nears its conclusion, the studio has released its "biggest (beta) patch yet", including a sweep of major additions.

As per MegaCrit's v0.113.0 patch notes, the headliner is The Fool; Slay the Spire 2's first new character, who's described as a "silly musician who wields a bow". Unsurprisingly, The Fool doesn't arrive in their final form, and the studio says it expects to make a "great number of content and balance changes" before the character is ready for the main branch.

Accompanying The Fool are two new game modes: Blitz and Dread. Blitz is described as a "condensed and chaotic" mode focused on deckbuilding. Unlocked after completing an Ascension run of any difficulty, it comes with five levels of Ascension shared across all characters. "The Merchant's wares feel a bit off," MegaCrit teases, "the map is gone, and Gold no longer matters??"

If you're looking for a more gruelling challenge, though, there's the "brutally difficult" new Dread mode, designed for players who've reached Ascension 10 on all characters, including The Fool. All ascension modifiers are enabled, according to MegaCrit, while bosses are stronger and buff all enemies found across their Act. And if that's still not enough to get your heart racing, MegaCrit notes curses will also pile up as you climb the Spire.

Beyond the headline stuff, v0.113.0 tweaks rest sites so they appear one floor earlier every act, and that's alongside the usual list of UI changes, art additions, nerfs, balance adjustments, and more. Full patch notes can be found on Steam.

Those players eager to put Slay the Spire 2's latest additions through their paces will need to enable the beta branch by right-clicking on Slay the Spire 2 in their Steam library and navigating to Properties > Game Versions & Betas and selecting 'public-beta' from the dropdown menu. MegaCrit notes the game's main branch has also been updated with all content and changes from the previous beta.

Just before VisionQuest resurrected Scarlet Witch in a surprise post-credits scene, the show snuck in a hidden Easter egg referencing Wanda Maximoff.

The reference is concealed in Billy Maximoff's jacket, and it was shared online by costume designer Sarah Young. On the denim jacket, a drawing of the Scarlet Witch crown can be seen. Check it out below.

Wiccan has added Scarlet Witch’s crown to his jacket in ‘VISIONQUEST’ (via sarahyoung_costumedesign | IG) https://t.co/m9XhoBR230November 18, 2026

The VisionQuest finale brought the family together, with Tommy Shepherd, Billy Maximoff, and Vision reuniting – though, as far as they all knew, Wanda remained dead. However, the post-credits scene revealed she was resurrected by Doctor Doom, who plans to make use of her powers.

"That's Downey's voice," VisionQuest showrunner Terry Matalas has shared of the moment. "I can't talk too much about how it was constructed, because I don't want to give away, but yes, that line was designed for this moment, specifically," he explained.

What Avengers: Doomsday might have in store for Wanda remains to be seen, but, for now, this VisionQuest Easter egg is a bittersweet reminder that the family is missing a member.

Doomsday features a supersized cast, including the likes of Anthony Mackie's Captain America, the Fantastic Four, the Thunderbolts, Letitia Wright's Shuri, Chris Hemsworth's Thor, the Fox-era X-Men, Chris Evans's Steve Rogers, and, of course, Robert Downey Jr.'s Doctor Doom.

#3926. GTA 6 First-Person Glitch Discovered, And It Works On Xbox & PS5

As you probably know, GTA 6 is not a game that's designed to let you freely play in first-person (at least not at launch), but thanks to some sleuthing from various GTA fans, it's been discovered that you can actually play this way.

This is thanks to a glitch that occurs when you change a specific setting and then spam the "View" button (formerly known as the "Back" button) on Xbox to trick the game into forcing you into first-person mode.

Here's how you do it (at your own risk - this is not an intended feature!):

The same instructions apply if you're on PS5, but it's the touchpad rather than the View button.

I've only been messing with this glitch a little bit so far, but it's pretty insane at first glance. You can run around, drive vehicles... do whatever you want to do. The only problem is that you can't actually back out of first-person once you're in it, although it seems some situations (like being arrested or going into a hair salon) will force you back into third-person.

So, why is Rockstar hiding this feature from us? It's probably because it's still in a work-in-progress, and there are some items that don't seem to function properly with the first-person viewpoint yet. This does seem to indicate a first-person perspective is in the works though, similar to how it was added into GTA 5 later down the line.

I'll leave you with some very, very quick screengrabs of my own down below, along with a helpful video that's getting a ton of traction on YouTube explaining how to make it work.

#3925. One week from launch, GTA 6's physical map reportedly leaks online thanks to the £350 collector's edition on show in a UK department store

With less than a week to go before GTA 6's hugely anticipated release, the game's final map - or at least a stylised poster version of it, depicting the state of Leonida's key landmarks - has surfaced online. It was reportedly snapped during Selfridge's sizable GTA 6's takeover, and is seemingly the physical map included in Rockstar's £350 collector's edition.

Fans have been pondering GTA 6's map for some time now, cross-referencing previous map leaks with official trailer footage in an attempt to gain some insight into the major landmarks and regions Rockstar has in store. And while the newly leaked map is far from granular, it does at least appear to confirm Leonida's rough layout and the key locations players can visit this time.

Assuming the map's veracity, it's all rendered in an art style somewhere between mid-century tourism poster and Adult Swim, featuring the phrase "The Goodtime State" up top - a riff on the actual Florida's nickname, The Sunshine State - while Leonida's most notable points of interest are interspersed with cartoon figures.

There's a toking turtle (or possibly a tortoise - I'm no expert), a golfer proudly wearing assless chaps, a flying saucer, and more. I'll spare you the geographic details confirmed on the map in case you want to go in unspoiled. One point of amusement though: the way the map photo is cropped means fans searching for confirmation of an in-game Key West are still none the wiser.

It's not entirely clear where the wonkily angled photo originated from, but prominent Rockstar Games community insider Videotech, who shared the image on social media, suggested it came from a "naughty Selfridges employee" during Selfridges' GTA 6 takeover. The map itself appears to be the "double-Sided souvenir poster with map of Leonida" included in Rockstar's eyewateringly expensive GTA 6 Collector's Edition. This costs £350 and doesn't come with a copy of the game. Or assless chaps, for that matter.

This isn't the first time GTA 6's map - officially said to be twice the size of GTA 5's - has leaked online, although previous leaks have been notably more controversial. Earlier this year, a group calling itself CyberLeek shared unofficial gameplay and map details in the name of what it called "Gamers' Rights". In August, with Netflix's official GTA 6 unveiling looming, the group cashed out nearly £200,000 from its crypto scheme.

Amid all this, Rockstar has been embroiled in legal action after it was accused of union busting following the firing of over 30 employees. The case's conclusion has been delayed until next week, meaning a verdict could arrive just as GTA 6 goes on sale.

#3924. Wolverine PS5's Sales Absolutely Plunged in October

Marvel’s Wolverine may have started strong in September’s Circana sales report, but it plunged in October.

Sony’s big PS5 exclusive for 2026, which attracted reasonable if utterly unremarkable reviews, ranked 14th in the latest US best-sellers list – dropping dramatically from first position the month of its release.

The game is now 15th overall for 2026 as a whole, down from 11th position in September. It’ll continue to fall with juggernauts like GTA 6 now officially out.

Couple other notes: Marvel's Wolverine dropped from 1st in Sept to 14th in Oct, ranks in top 15 YTD. On the YTD charts, less than $10M separates 8th place from 13th - it's a tight cluster.

The exclusive’s lore accurate lack of legs can likely be attributed to the game’s worse than expected reviews.

While it’s not universally disliked – we awarded it an 8/10, after all – fans understandably expect better from dev Insomniac.

Sony’s running discounts on the game during Black Friday to try and stimulate some enthusiasm around it, and I suspect this may be one of those titles that ends up in a lot of hardware bundles in the future.

To be fair, the platform holder seemed relatively satisfied with the title’s 2.4 million sales during its recent financial report.

I suppose it’s possible the launch numbers really did meet its expectations, but it may now be disappointed with the title’s long-term momentum – or lack thereof.

We’ll probably have to wait until its next investor update before we get more information.

GTA 6's fake Instagram shitposts, which include Rockstar Games clowning on how long the game took to release, are proving to be a highlight of the whole experience for many.

GTA games are generally developed as a time capsule of what culture was like at the time, so while GTA 5 definitely had some social media influence in it, things have certainly changed in the time since that game was released 13 years ago.

GTA 6 on the other hand goes all in, with takes on WhatsApp, Instagram, and a Shazam for cars called WAInk. On top of that, when you go to bed in-game, Jason doesn't go to sleep – he instead starts looking at the phone and scrolling aimlessly.

But since 2013, social media shitposting has become the norm, and GTA 6's version of Instagram is shockingly accurate. Real social media has been filled with screenshots of the posts found on Snapmatic, with Rockstar's famous attention to detail shining through.

Highlights of my own playthrough have been an image of a Batman-esque hero holding down a villain with the caption "me when I find the guy who shit my pants," a woman looking seductive with the caption "how the emergency door latch looks at me on the plane," while real social media highlights abstract memes and a certified @mr.queef classic: a speedometer maxed out with "me when I get a call that my wife is giving birth (I'm omw to the casino)."

However, Rockstar has also poked fun at itself through this meme onslaught, with its own take on the "we got x before GTA 6 meme." One post shows a Paw Patrol-like game titled Barnyard Blue Hot Fursuit with the caption, "Barnyard Blue video game before Race and Chase 7 is crazy." Another shows the different types of headaches, with a full head one captioned with "Race and Chase 7 delayed another year."

Funnily enough, Race'n'Chase was the original name for the game in development that would eventually become Grand Theft Auto. So basically, Rockstar made the first "we got x before GTA 7" joke.

#3922. A new report reckons 40% of developers in the video games industry are using generative AI - but even more think it's harmful

"I did not get into a creative industry to hand over the creativity to an algorithm."

Despite all the outrage and criticism around game developers and publishers using generative AI in gaming, a new report from the Game Developers Conference (GDC) calculates that as many as 40 percent of developers active in the industry use the controversial tools in their work. This is up four percent compared to the same report last year.

That's according to the latest State of the Game Industry report from GDC, which gathers data from more than 2,300 respondents including, but not limited to, game industry professionals, made up of developers, producers, marketers, executives, and investors.

The report notes that 57 percent of developers who say they do use it, use gen-AI for "text generation, research, early prototyping, coding, and presentations". There appears to be a big split between triple-A studios that use gen-AI (with 27 percent of triple-A developers noting that they "feel encouraged or pressured" to use it) and indie devs, of which only nine percent say the same. Perhaps unsurprisingly - given how vocally against gen-AI a lot of 'frontline developers' have been - the tools are mostly used by "business operations and services, mobile-only studios, and free-to-play developers".

There seems to be a gap in the ages of those willing to use AI tools as well; per the report, over half (54 percent) of people 45 years or older reported using the tools - an eight-point increase from last year's survey. There is also more usage among men (45 percent) than women (33 percent).

What is perhaps more striking is that more people responded to the survey saying that they think AI is having a negative impact on games (55 percent) than responded saying they use the tech, suggesting a trend of caution rather than widespread adoption. Notably, respondents saying they are wary of the technology increased one percent since last year, so more people think AI is having a negative effect on the industry now than at the same time in 2025. Perhaps that's because of the sweeping layoffs we've seen across the games industry, often mentioned in the same breath as AI. Or the 'AI slop' that's been flooding Steam and pushing more traditional developers out. Orr some of the abysmal projects we've seen launch that have clearly used gen-AI assets.

"I did not get into a creative industry to hand over the creativity to an algorithm," said one respondent from the UK when explaining why they don't use gen-AI tools. "I got into this industry to collaborate with creative people, not to have an advanced chatbot riff on the ideas of someone who was laid off," said another from California. "I believe that no one should have to read what no human has written and shouldn't have to see what no human has created," said yet another from Minnesota.

The use of generative AI remains controversial in the games industry, though with big companies like Epic and Microsoft doubling down on the tech, it seems this split between developers that want to embrace it and those that don't is only growing larger.

#3921. Crimson Desert studio is implementing AI "throughout our entire development pipeline," and expects DokeV to launch in 2028

"This enables a more efficient allocation of development resources and enhances overall production speed."

Crimson Desert and DokeV developer Pearl Abyss is planning to further integrate generative AI into its workflow.

The South Korean studio said as much in its latest quarterly Earnings Letter, explaining that it had previously "validated game systems only after implementing them manually." Now, Pearl Abyss is using AI "to rapidly validate diverse design concepts prior to actual implementation," and argues the move "enables a more efficient allocation of development resources and enhances overall production speed."

"However, AI serves strictly as a tool to support concept validation and pipeline productivity, while the core gameplay experience and actual content creation remain fully driven by our development team," the developer said.

When Crimson Desert first launched, players spotted a crop of suspicious in-game images that looked like they were prompted into existence. Pearl Abyss soon explained that some "2D visual props" were generated with AI tools, but were always intended to be replaced with human-made art, before quickly patching them out of the hit open-world game.

It seems Pearl Abyss is now even more keen on the controversial tech, however: "We are integrating AI technologies to enhance development productivity and overall quality. AI is being utilized across various stages of development - including the automation of repetitive tasks, content creation support, and test optimization - and we are expanding its implementation throughout our entire development pipeline. We view AI not as a substitute for human developers, but as a tool to elevate development efficiency and quality. We will continue to expand our application of AI to deliver higher-fidelity games to the market more expeditiously."

Elsewhere in the letter, the studio said its previously announced creature-collector DokeV is "targeting a launch in the second half of 2028" and we should hear more about it within the year. DokeV was initially targeting a 2023 launch a few years ago. Meanwhile, Crimson Desert is being prepped for a Nintendo Switch 2 launch "in the first half of next year."

The use of generative AI in game development has been a hot topic for years, though it's only become more prevalent in recent months as 'AI slop' floods Steam and big companies like Epic Games proudly adopt the tech. A recent report even estimated that around 40 percent of active developers use AI tools in their work.

As someone who's been covering both Lego and the sale for many years, I'm genuinely impressed at the spread this early in the game. Plenty of top-tier models have already reached record lows (as demonstrated by the Editor's choice picks above), and unlike usual, the best offers aren't limited to one region. Typically, the UK gets the lion's share of amazing price cuts - and while Britain is still enjoying some particularly good bargains you won't find anywhere else, I'm taken aback at how the US is keeping up this year. Fans in the States will find plenty of legitimately great savings right now, on collector's display models to playsets. This bodes well as the sale continues to pick up steam.

In terms of the models I'm looking out for, I'm keeping a particularly close eye out for big 2026 releases like the Pokemon range and Donkey Kong Arcade. While very recent launches (such as the new Batman Returns Batmobile) are very unlikely to get a price cut, I'm hopeful that slightly older ones will. While I suspect discounts on the most headline-grabbing sets (Minas Tirith, say) will be reserved for Black Friday, plenty of the others are already getting reductions. What you want to keep an eye out for are early Black Friday deal badges to guarantee the price across the sale or record low prices. I typically use Camelcamelcamel for this, as it tracks price history on Amazon including averages.

Want some pointers on what to look out for? Personally, I'll never click through to checkout on a product unless I've specifically looked into its price history. Price comparison sites like Camelcamelcamel are brilliant for this, because they allow you to see historic highs and lows across the product's lifespan at Amazon - and this is usually indicative of other retailers too. You'll see record lows as well as average costs here, so can make a more informed decision as a result.

Speaking of Amazon, beware of the retailer (or those like it) artificially increasing the price of something before the sale. If the cost of an item suddenly skyrockets, that's probably because it's going to get a big discount and the hike is to make any ensuing reduction seem bigger. Don't fall for it, always check price history to ensure you're getting a decent deal!

Hey everyone! I'm locked in to track the best early Lego Black Friday deals ahead of the full sale later next week, and there are plenty of offers to keep us busy. Both the US and UK have some excellent discounts to speak of, from older kits to new 2026 kits.

#3919. The Sunday Papers

The Sunday Papers is our weekly roundup of great writing about (mostly) videogames from across the web.

While following a peculiar trail of silver and saffron leaves around the largest roots of the Treehouse, you come across a hexagonal wooden door lying half-hidden among ivy and moss. Scraping away the dirt, you discover a faint, absurd engraving of a newspaper. What mystery is here? You turn the brass knob – strange, it is warm! – and the engraving of the newspaper flutters. The pages turn faster and faster, emitting a howling gale that bowls you head over foot. When you pick yourself up, you are inside a vast attic full of books and bricabrac, lit from one side by windows that offer no view of the outside world – just light and mist.

Tarnation! You have been lured into the eternal prison of Sunday Afternoon. Fortunately, there are several ways to escape. Each of the arcane objects before you is secretly a portal, transporting you to another site of arcane activity, in a bizarre web of diversions that cannot possibly reflect the hand of a human curator. Which will you choose?

As you step forward, your toe nudges an ornamental scroll. It growls and wriggles like a panicking caterpillar, scooting away under a table. Before you lose sight of it, you discern the title and subject of the text – it's an essay by Kyle Tam about the yokai of Promise Mascot Agency.

Deep in a drawer, you discover a sour-smelling binder full of extracts from an ancient and all but indecipherable dispute over the discovery of "generative AI" in something called "Big Walk". The stakes are long-buried, but many of the individual pieces of writing are lively. Here is Bruno Dias noting in passing that "one of the harms of the 'AI' political project is the propaganda machine dedicated to making you feel stupid and helpless." Here is a professorial interjection from Brendan Keogh calling on the warring parties to recognise when "critiques of generative AI are actually just deflected critiques of the capitalist relations of technology and labour". Here is Mike Cook arguing that "what's happening is not unusual, it's not extreme, it's not unfair and it's not a 'public flogging'." Here is a ticker tape message from Hannah Nicklin observing that "if your radical position doesn’t have room for transformation it will not be safe until it contains just you".

A footnote in the same dusty sheaf of papers points you towards another work from Mike Cook in a different drawer. This one consists of neon slides, slotted into an antique View-Master, and explores a comparison between procedural generation and street photography.

Peering at the weirdly white and opaque windowpanes, you realise there are intricate equations traced in the condensation. It appears to be a post-mortem for a "post-cosy" game called Danchi Days, in which developer Melos Han-Tani discusses wishlist conversion rates and the problem of not fitting neatly into any recognisable genre.

A snowglobe stands on a mantelpiece, the flakes still orbiting a miniature washtub as though the object had been recently shaken, even though the chamber has clearly been abandoned for decades. You put it to your ear, anticipating the faint jingle of Xmas bells. Instead, you are almost deafened by a screeching guitar chord. Here is Erin Keane to explain.

Next to the snowglobe on the mantelpiece, there's a souvenir shop conch shell, polished to a high sheen. You put that to your ear, hoping to catch the soothing shuffle of surf on shingle, and a disembodied voice tells you to piss off. Tim Sniffen has some thoughts about gentrification, and why only he should be allowed to do it.

Again, one of these mystic artefacts hides the key to your release from the suffocating stillness of Sunday Afternoon. Which will you choose? Or have you, perhaps, brought a sorcerous teleportation device of your own? Please share. Here is Joanna Newsom's Cosmia to help you think.

#3918. Interest in The Legend of Zelda was "getting smaller and smaller" before Breath of the Wild, according to former Nintendo marketing leads

The Legend of Zelda was in "dire straits" before Breath of the Wild gave the beloved series a massive second wind, according to two former Nintendo marketing leads.

The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time's most recent remake has been a mega success, becoming the fastest-selling Switch 2 game so far, but the shiny new adventure has also prompted some online debate over where the series should go next. Should Zelda lean into its carefully directed history - like the one brilliantly remade in Ocarina of Time - or keep the ball rolling with Breath of the Wild's wide open, spontaneous sandbox?

Nintendo of America's ex-director of social media marketing Kit Ellis and former public relations manager Krysta Yang chimed in on the discourse in their latest podcast (below), and explained that Zelda wasn't doing too hot before the Switch era.

"There has been some revisionist history out there lately," Ellis said in response to fans who reckon "the Zelda team ripped away" series staples, like classic dungeons and linear worlds, at the height of their popularity.

"I remember, I was going to the focus groups where it was a really dark moment," Ellis continued. "The feedback was like, 'The fan base is dwindling. This is not bringing in new players.'"

The Legend of Zelda was supposedly "shrinking," while "interest in the audience was getting smaller and smaller" with each new entry. "They had to do something dramatic," Ellis said.

"This series was in dire straits. They were selling, like, nothing," Yang added.

The Zelda series was certainly never irrelevant, but there's a pretty big gap between the roughly 8m copies Twilight Princess sold at the beginning of the Wii generation, the roughly 3m copies Skyward Sword sold at the end of the console's life, and the 34m copies that Breath of the Wild sold just one console generation later.

It was a success so big it spawned a wildly ambitious sequel, Tears of the Kingdom, and even influenced the latest 2D Zelda, Echoes of Wisdom. Now that classic Zelda's back in the spotlight, though, I do hope Nintendo's able to slot the series' curated dungeons into whatever the next mainline game becomes.

Exclusive: Francis Lawrence breaks down Suzanne Collins's behind the scenes involvement in The Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping

When you purchase through links on our site, we may earn an affiliate commission. Here’s how it works.

Hunger Games Suzanne Collins doesn't take a backseat to the movies, according to Sunrise on the Reaping director Francis Lawrence.

Before the latest novel was even published, it was confirmed a film adaptation would also be in the works, telling the prequel story of Haymitch Abernathy – the District 12 victor who went on to mentor Katniss Everdeen and Peeta Mellark.

"Yeah, she's very involved," Lawrence tells us when we meet with him in London to discuss The Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping. "When she sends the manuscript, I read it, usually a couple times, and then the first thing we do is we sit in a conference room at the publishing company that she works through, and we break down the book together. And we've done that since Catching Fire.

"And then she's on the phone with me and Nina [Jacobson, producer] and the screenwriter every day for hours, probably hundreds of hours of calls talking through the script, and then she kind of disappears when we shoot," he continues. "And then we bring her back in when we have a cut, and she looks at the cut, and we give her the data on tests, and we decide if we have to do any pickups or anything. And then she obviously sees the finished product, so she is very, very involved. She's just not there on the shoot, and part of that is so that she can keep an objective perspective on it for when she sees the cut."

While the Sunrise on the Reaping film has yet to be released to the public, it's already garnered strongly positive reactions from fans, which kicked off with an outpouring of love for each casting announcement.

"It's wishy-washy with things online, and I feel like, in this day and age, it is a lot easier to be negative, and I feel like the negativity is always a little bit louder," says McKenna Grace, who plays District 12 tribute Maysilee Donner. "And so, it's such a blessing whenever you're a part of a fan base, or whenever anything that you're a part of is getting positivity, and for it to be such an overwhelming, kind response, I feel like is just… But it's just been so wonderful that they're happy with it, and that they're accepting us into this franchise."

Joseph Zada, who plays Haymitch, adds: "And even a lot of the people that have been able to see it from press that haven't been fans, or haven't seen the previous films, are just also so excited to see it, which is such a scary thing. [You] walk into a prequel hoping that it can stand alone, and that people that aren't familiar with the franchise can enjoy the film, too."

The Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping hits theaters this November 20. In the meantime, check out our The Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping review and our guide to all the biggest movie release dates.

#3916. The Blood of Dawnwalker is getting a New Game Plus mode in next week's update

UPDATE 17TH NOVEMBER: The Blood of Dawnwalker update 1.2 - the update that brings a New Game Plus mode, predominantly - is now available on PC, PS5, and Xbox Series S/X.

New Game Plus, as mentioned below, raises the level cap to 100, and scales enemies and regions in the game around you. Previously, the game was zone-scaled, so some zones were tougher than others. In New Game Plus, this will no longer be the case, so you can go and explore Xanthe's region at the back of Vale Sangora straight away, if you want to.

There'll be new versions of equipment with new stats to find, and they'll be labelled with "NG+" so you know when you've picked one up. You can unlock New Game Plus from the main menu after choosing your base save and difficulty option. All of your accrued skill perks and abilities will be available to you at the start of the Withering Away quest in the game's prologue.

The full patch notes for Dawnwalker update 1.2 are:

ORIGINAL STORY 13TH NOVEMBER: A New Game Plus mode is coming to vampiric RPG The Blood of Dawnwalker next week.

Developer Rebel Wolves has now detailed everything coming with The Blood of Dawnwalker's Update 1.2, currently planned to go live sometime next week, and top of the list of changes is a New Game Plus for players who have already rolled credits on the game.

"If you completed the Epilogue, you can dive right back into Vale Sangora with New Game+," the developer revealed earlier today. "Your level, skills, and inventory will carry over." Rebel Wolves is upping the level cap to 100 for New Game Plus, which will also have items with updated stats and enemies "balanced and scaled uniformly across all regions."

Elsewhere in Update 1.2, the studio is making tweaks to "enemy health pools and how often they use their abilities during combat," and improving terrain geometry to allow for "smoother movement during combat and exploration." We'll need to wait for more comprehensive patch notes before finding out which enemies are getting spongier or flimsier, however.

While the incoming patch doesn't seem to be as beefy as the last - the one that added animal petting and an easier Story mode - it'll be a good way to sink your teeth deeper into a game that's already begging to be replayed, thanks to a time management mechanic that can drastically change any given run.

The new game from some former The Witcher 3 veterans came out in September and seems to have been a hit. Eurogamer's The Blood of Dawnwalker review called the game a "familiar dark fantasy adventure, but one with bold and provocative ideas of its own, that's mostly, enormously successful."

I've said it before, and I'll say it again; Lego Rivendell is, in my opinion, one of (if not the) best Lego sets around. Even with more modern rivals like Minas Tirith or Barad-dur, I don't think any of them manage to blend spectacle with diorama-style interiors as well as this kit does.

Modelled after the elven refuge as it appears in Fellowship of the Ring, this kit is a sprawling recreation of the Last Homely House; with over 6,000 pieces to play with, it can create a level of depth and detail most kits can't hope to match. This is the kind of Lego set where you'll discover something new every time you stop to admire it. Lego Rivendell is also impressive enough on display that it'll draw a "woah" worthy of Owen Wilson from most onlookers.

This model often enjoys a price cut in time for the annual Lego Black Friday deals, but this time it's been given an even bigger saving. Actually, it's dropped to an all-time low price that we haven't seen before. Usually, the best we can expect is a reduction down to £365.

There are four distinct areas for Lego Rivendell; the main house with its tower and display showing off the broken shards of Narsil, the council area with its ring of seats and plinth for the One Ring, a bridge leading to Arwen's pergola, and a woodland smithy where the elves are busy creating masterworks at the forge. Many of these have a mix of exposed and hidden areas you can reveal by lifting off the lid, which really sells the dollhouse-like experience here.

The top half of the tower can be removed to show the room where Bilbo Baggins is staying, for instance, and there's a desk set up where he's writing in his memoirs. (Yes, his minifigure has an alternate face so you can recreate that moment as well - shudder). Meanwhile, Arwen's pergola is removable so that you can get a good look at the forge beneath. Oh, and as for the council area? Well, let's just say Sauron's eye is firmly fixed on this meeting...

Then there are the minifigures. Premium Lego sets like this often come with a lot of figs, but Rivendell feels particularly generous. There are 15 in total; Frodo, Sam, Merry, Pippin, Gandalf, Aragorn, Legolas, Gimli, Boromir, Elrond, Arwen, Bilbo, a couple of elves, and a visiting dwarf. That's enough to make the whole kit feel positively alive, and you can recreate a whole host of moments from the movie if you'd like.

I shouldn't skip over the fact that it's downright beautiful to look at, either. Whether it's the tasteful pastel tiles, the abundance of flora carpeting the grounds, or the autumnal trees looming over it all, Lego Rivendell is an incredibly handsome centerpiece.

It looks like the majority of Lego Lord of the Rings kits are on offer right now; the Balrog Book Nook, Sauron's Helmet, Barad-dur, and Minas Tirith have all been heavily reduced in price at Amazon.

Even with the arrival of Lego Minas Tirith earlier this year (which just got its first discount, by the way), I still don't think Rivendell has been surpassed. Yes, the Gondorian city is jaw-dropping. For one thing, it's very cleverly designed with a forced perspective using multiple scales. For another, it's striking in a way Rivendell isn't; a mass of white walls and towers surround the spur of a mountain, drawing every eye in the room. However (and this is no insult to Minas Tirith - I'm currently in the middle of building it), I still think Rivendell is prettier and has more 'going on' under the surface.

Basically, I'd always point to this kit if someone asked me what I thought the best ever Lego set was - it's captured both my heart and my imagination, just like its inspiration did when I first saw it on-screen in 2001.

In terms of other Lego news, it looks like there will be 10 Lego Star Wars concept art minifigures for the 50th anniversary.

When you purchase through links on our site, we may earn an affiliate commission. Here’s how it works.

Even though Grand Theft Auto 6 will be taking over the world tomorrow, World of Warcraft: Forever was the first game this month that people flocked to in record-breaking numbers.

While we don't know the exact player count like we do with games on Steam, we can make an educated guess on just how many people dove into the MMO via a recent set of statistics from Blizzard. According to the official WoW X account, over 15 million characters were created in the last few weeks.

Characters aren't individual players. You can create dozens of characters on your account if you want to, but I'd guess most people didn't do that. This is a game where you can put hundreds of hours into one character before ever reaching the level cap. There definitely aren't 15 million total players based on this statistic, but the number might not be massively below that.

I can't say I'm surprised that a spin-off MMO that will remain stuck in the most universally nostalgic era of WoW was a big hit. Everyone who stopped playing for one reason or another came back to remember what it was like to smack a scorpion for 38 seconds.

Whether or not they'll stick around is the question. Blizzard plans on updating the game with new things to do for players at different stages of the long leveling journey. Most people are still weeks away from reaching the level 60 cap, partially because there are so many things to do that don't involve XP. The first raid is around the corner, but I'm curious to see what kind of stuff is added for those of us who are still chilling in the mid-30s. It'd better be good because many of us will be on vacation in Leonida for the next several weeks.

#3913. "We've finally reached this milestone": Cyberpunk 2077 multiplayer mod CyberMP kicks off open beta after around six years preparing for cybermayhem

"Let's see how the project handles real player traffic"

After a couple of years of regular testing behind closed doors, Cyberpunk 2077 multiplayer mod CyberMP is now out in open beta, giving anyone who fancies a bit of multi-merc action a chance to give it a go. Though, if you do, be prepared for bugs and crashes, as work on the mod is far from over with the release of this "true beta".

As shown off in the video above, CyberMP's not about being able to play through the base game's missions with friends, but rather cruise around Night City as a gang getting into races and PvP shootouts. In that regard, it seems more akin to GTA 4's online mode than GTA 5's, with classic improvised hijinks the main draw over being able to pull off gigs with a crew. Though, there do also look to be roleplaying servers which could scratch the itch of those more interested in pretending to be a merc than blowing up other people's rides.

"After almost six years of development, countless reworks, and code rewrites, we're finally launching the public beta," the modders wrote on Discord. "Anyone can jump in and play now — no invites or applications needed. Fair warning: this is a true beta. Crashes, desyncs, and server drops under heavy load are completely normal for now. That's exactly why we need testers. We welcome everyone: regular players, future server admins, and those who just love breaking game mechanics."

"Right now, our absolute priority is stability and fixing crashes," they continued later in the post. "New features are planned, but we need to polish the foundation first. A huge thank you to everyone who has been with us since the early versions, helped with closed testing, and patiently waited. We've finally reached this milestone. Let's see how the project handles real player traffic!"

According to the modders, CyberMP's "client doesn't have a digital signature yet", which could cause antivirus software not to be a fan of it. They're also anticipating "problems with the anti‑cheat system", so it may be worth holding off on giving the mod a go if you're not keen on being trolled by someone with the sort of destructive power usually reserved for megacorps and AIs from beyond the blackwall in the Cyberpunkverse.

For info on how to get CyberMP up and running, as well as create a custom server dedicated to the likes of roleplay or races, head over to its website. As you might expect, the mod requires a legit copy of Cyberpunk bought on either Steam, GOG, or the Epic store.

#3912. Magic: The Gathering animated series Planeswalker is coming to Netflix in 2027

Netflix's long-gestating Magic: The Gathering animated series is called Planeswalker, and it's coming in 2027.

The title was revealed at MagicCon Atlanta, and Netflix shared a first look at the show on Twitter/X on 13th November. "Every great story begins with a spark. Here's your first look at Planeswalker, a new animated series based on Magic: The Gathering. Coming to Netflix in 2027", the company wrote, and shared a teaser, which you can see below:

According to a synopsis shared with IGN, the series follows Chandra Nalaar, "a volatile pyromancer hunted for her gifts, and haunted by her past". It continues: "Confronted by an insidious force, Chandra and some of the most legendary Planeswalkers must harness their extraordinary abilities, navigate treacherous alliances, and battle their own inner demons to prevent a cataclysmic war that threatens to consume their very existence".

Netflix first announced a Magic: The Gathering series in June 2019, with Avengers: Endgame directors Joe and Anthony Russo attached, and it was originally due in late 2022. Two years in, the original showrunners departed over creative differences, and in September 2024, Netflix confirmed it had started again from scratch with Star Trek: Picard and 12 Monkeys showrunner Terry Matalas in charge.

IGN reports that Matalas, who most recently ran Marvel's VisionQuest, is running the show alongside Cindy Appel. Budapest-based studio DIGIC Pictures is handling the animation.

At the end of last month, we learned PUBG is also being turned into a live-action series for Netflix, with Donald Glover set to direct, write, executive produce, and star.

Glover is a two-time Emmy and Golden Globe winner, best known for Atlanta and Community. Krafton calls PUBG "one of the world’s most enduring gaming franchises", and says the game, which is credited with popularising the battle royale genre, holds seven Guinness World Records.

It's why Jennifer Svedberg-Yen's setting up an investment fund

When you purchase through links on our site, we may earn an affiliate commission. Here’s how it works.

Clair Obscur: Expedition 33's writer and Sandfall Interactive's former narrative lead, Jennifer Svedberg-Yen, thinks the game industry is "eating itself" and "losing so much institutional knowledge" through mass layoffs and studio closures.

"I look around the game industry. A lot of what's happening really breaks my heart. I feel that the industry is eating itself. I feel that we are losing so much institutional knowledge. We're making it extraordinarily difficult for a younger generation of developers to have formative experiences. There's so much disruption in the industry right now," she says in an interview with GamesBeat.

"I come from an investment background. My original background was in private equity. I've seen that side. It frustrates me, because I think about it as, to use an agricultural analogy – in the past we've over-harvested the soil. We've tried to extract everything we can from the land. What we really need to do is cultivate the land. We need stewardship over the land. That means not over-harvesting. That means reinvesting in the land, in making sure there are nutrients put back into the land, so we can grow bigger and better things. I feel that we are not doing that as an industry," she adds.

Svedberg-Yen's not content with watching the chaos unfold, though. The award-winning writer is now working to set up a narrative investment fund to help developers along "between the seed stage and going to publishers." As she explains, many smaller creators need to develop a demo before pitching their games to publishers. "But to make a demo you need money. To get money you have to go to publishers." Her investment fund will hopefully help devs crack the "chicken and egg question," and minimize risk at the earliest stages of production.

"I'm not trying to compete with publishers," she says. "But I'm trying to find a way to work with them to get us back on solid ground. Above all, I really would like to champion other people and other creatives to have a chance to pursue their dreams, have a chance to make the games they want to make."

Svedberg-Yen's comments come during a devastating year for the games industry. Xbox plans to reduce its headcount by 3,200 by next summer. Sony shuttered Bluepoint Games and made layoffs at Sucker Punch. EA closed BioWare after a whopping three-decade run. Tomb Raider studio Crystal Dynamics laid off workers for the sixth time since its last full game. Even the most acclaimed developers are still at risk, and keeping track of all the layoffs in 2026 alone would likely require a dedicated Excel sheet.

Clair Obscur: Expedition 33 has sold 8.7 million copies and made $366 million, analyst says, and that's despite the "Game Pass cannibalization."

It's here. GTA 6 has been loosed upon the world, and another nation's productivity goes dark as each advancing hour unleashes midnight unlocks on the next timezone. And hey, from the sounds of it, people seem to like what they're finding—and they're finding a lot.

You can mini-golf. You can go on beach dates. You can text and drive (don't). You can doomscroll, and birdwatch, and ride a jetski with a dog. GTA 6 is dense with possible activities, actions, systems, and mechanics, but not everyone is having the best luck navigating the maelstrom of associated controls and button prompts. Allow me to present Japanese X user @Shunep3_STS, who on this day represents all of us:

操作が増えて覚えきれず、間違えて２つ買ったシェイクをしゃがみ歩きしながら飲み干すヤバい奴になってる https://t.co/OLXaEQGc7CNovember 18, 2026

"There are so many new controls I can’t keep them all straight," said @Shunep3_STS via machine translation, "and now I’m that guy chugging two shakes I accidentally bought while walking around in a squat."

There's something magical about this image. To begin with, the scene—like all of GTA 6—looks profoundly, almost grotesquely expensive: the delicate feathering of Jason's forearm hair, the pseudo-memoji of Cal in the text message notification, the fidelity of pebbled sand that probably cost more to realize in-game than I've spent on rent in the last three years. It's a tableau of technological excess.

And all of that's being deployed to present a man double-fisting slushies in an empty parking lot as he skulks like an imperiled raccoon. Look at him! Look at his face! He's got his chiseled jaw set like he's Solid Snake, but he's nursing a tummy full of iced corn syrup because the pilot controlling his body got too overwhelmed by which buttons do what.

And he's not alone: Our own Andrea Shearon is one of the many struggling to keep up with the sheer volume of button prompts in GTA 6. "There's so much going on," she said. "I just walk up to people and kind of mash all the face buttons for a surprise. You never know if I'm gonna punch someone or do squats or flip them off."

She's spent a lot of time accidentally making rude gestures at her snake as a result.

Keep up to date with the most important stories and the best deals, as picked by the PC Gamer team.

Amidst all the breathless praise, clips of psychopathic violence, reactionary outrage-mongering, and general noise coming out of GTA 6's launch, @Shunep3_STS's moment of shame feels very pure. It's a universal experience: No matter how much a game is hyped up, no matter how much money is spent on making it look as impressive as humanly and technologically possible, no matter how much we might want it to, we all inevitably find a way to fumble the controls so badly that the illusion entirely breaks down.

We're all, at some point, a man huddling in the dark, trying to figure out how to put down his sippy cups.

#3908. Call of Duty Endowment marks Remembrance Day with veterans' Valor Pack push

The Call of Duty Endowment is marking Remembrance Day and its 17th anniversary by encouraging Modern Warfare 4 and Warzone players to pick up its Valor Pack, with all of Activision's net proceeds going towards helping veterans find jobs.

The Call of Duty Endowment Valor Pack - which has been available since Modern Warfare 4 launched on 23rd October - was designed by the Endowment and Infinity Ward with US Marine Corps veteran and Medal of Honor recipient Kyle Carpenter in mind.

The items include a melee weapon blueprint inscribed with "Worth Fighting For", plus items called Relentless and Still Standing.

According to the Call of Duty blog, 100 percent of Activision's net proceeds from the pack (after VAT and sales tax) go to the Endowment.

To mark Remembrance Day, players who owned it and launched either game before 6pm GMT on 12th November also received double XP tokens and a DMZ survival kit.

"Veterans bring incredible skills into the workplace after military service," said Carpenter.

The Endowment, which supports veterans in the UK as well as the US, says it has now helped place more than 180,000 into "high-quality jobs", and wants to reach 200,000 by 2030.

Other partners are also raising money, with Pilot's round-up campaign raising more than £4.7 million ($6 million) for the Endowment since 2019. Polaris will also donate around £19,500 ($25,000) if players collectively complete 5 million rides in its DAGOR vehicle across Modern Warfare 4 and Warzone by 25th November.

It comes two weeks after Activision apologised to bereaved families of the Itaewon crowd crush victims and confirmed it would remove real footage of the tragedy from Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4. Players discovered that the game's opening cinematic uses short news clips to depict fictional civilian casualties during a North Korean invasion of South Korea. Those clips have since been found to include archive footage from the 2022 Itaewon disaster, in which around 160 people died.

Call of Duty's anti-cheat team Ricochet recently announced it's officially cracking down on Warzone Agent.

#3907. "Nobody was hurt" in shooting near Clockwork Revolution devs InXile Entertainment's office, the Xbox-owned studio and police confirm

"Nobody was hurt" in a shooting last week near the California office of Clockwork Revolution developers InXile, both the studio and local police have confirmed. The incident, which took place on November 11th, is currently being investigated and police have reportedly taken a suspect into custody.

"Officers got there [on November 11th]," Tustin police sergeant Christopher Peterson said in statement to Aftermath. "They responded to a report of a drive-by shooting there. Located multiple shell casings. Nobody was hurt. Processed the crime scene, and then sometime [Friday] morning, a little before 11 [AM], they took a suspect into custody. And the investigation is still kind of ongoing as to where and why."

"We’re relieved that no one was hurt at our inXile office," a spokesperson for InXile said in a separate statement. "Our focus is on supporting our team, and we are working closely with law enforcement as they investigate."

InXile are set to release steampunk RPG Clockwork Revolution next year. The studio, developers of the likes of Wasteland 3 and The Bard's Tale IV, are one of the few Xbox-owned studios not to have been affected - at least as of writing - by Microsoft's ongoing mass layoffs this year.

Since being announced in 2023, Clockwork Revolution's dripped with Bioshock-ish vibes and popped up semi-regularly at Xbox showcases. "Wield the power of an incredible device to travel back in time, changing the past and rewriting the future of the city you call home: the vibrant steampunk metropolis of Avalon," reads its Steam synopsis. "In this immersive RPG, you'll step into the shoes of Morgan Vanette, a fully customizable player-character and member of the Rotten Row Hooligans. Travel between past and present as you battle the ruthless Lady Ironwood, who has been manipulating time to keep the working class struggling while amassing immense wealth and power."

Best wishes to the staff at InXile, here's hoping that going forwards they're able to get with making what's looking to be an intriguingly funky game without enduring any more concerning incidents like this one.

Tom Hiddleston has revealed the call from Marvel bosses that proved to him how integral Loki was to Avengers: Doomsday.

"The call came from [Marvel Studios president] Kevin Feige and [co-president] Louis D'Esposito, and it was very clear there was no way of continuing a story about the multiverse without Loki," Hiddleston told Empire magazine. "They wanted me to be part of it. That's what they said."

Hiddleston also mentioned that the multiverse – a narrative concept now reaching critical mass thanks to the MCU – and Loki are effectively intertwined at this point, making the notion of ignoring the former trickster god all but impossible.

Hiddleston said, "At this point, having expanded what we can call the multiverse in a way that isn't a niche reference now, and Loki's position as the God of Stories, on the big chair at the End of Time, holding the branches of many timelines together, there was no way to continue to talk about the multiverse without acknowledging his position."

Away from Doomsday, the newfound God of Stories has also been a crucial component for Marvel's so-called 'Multiverse Saga', a sprawling chapter of MCU movies and shows that kicked off with WandaVision, Falcon and The Winter Soldier, and Loki in 2021, and culminating with Avengers: Secret Wars in 2027.

Loki has largely been at the forefront of the more multiverse-heavy adventures, inadvertently splintering the multiverse in Loki season 1, before acting as the force to hold them together in Loki season 2.

Loki also doorstepped Peggy Carter and Steve Rogers just after their iconic dance in Avengers: Endgame – as revealed during the new ending of Endgame's Encore re-release.

Of course, Loki isn't the only notable Marvel figure rocking up in Avengers: Doomsday. Far from it. Alongside him is Robert Downey Jr.'s Doctor Doom, Steve Rogers, plus the casts of Fantastic Four and Thunderbolts. Several OG Avengers are also on the scene, plus multiple members of Fox's X-Men team, including Professor X, Magneto, and Cyclops.

Avengers: Doomsday hits UK cinemas on December 16 and US cinemas on December 18.

For more, we've done our best TVA impression and untangled the Marvel timeline for you.

If I can pinpoint one disappointing aspect of GTA 6 that most will agree on, it's the fact that it runs at 30 fps.

Many of us remember when this was normal for consoles (especially the PS3/Xbox 360 era), but these days, it's unusual for a major game to not offer a 60 fps or 40 fps performance option. Unfortunately, even if you're rocking a PS5 Pro, GTA 6 moves at a filmic 30.

That's disappointing news for anyone who shelled out $900+ for the more powerful PS5 Pro expecting better performance (or vindicating news, if you're a PC Gamer reader waiting for the arbitrarily delayed PC version), but Rockstar insists there was no way around it.

Speaking to Kotaku, technology production director Marc Chambers explained that the current consoles just aren't powerful enough to keep up without significant compromises.

"Our base presentation makes use of ray-traced reflections and global illumination. On the PS5 Pro, this is enhanced with the addition of ray-traced shadows, as well as overall added clarity through the use of PlayStation Spectral Super Resolution (PSSR)," he said. "The PS5 Pro features an upgraded graphics processor and upscaling technology that we leverage to increase the game’s visual fidelity. While the PS5 Pro’s central processor is slightly better than the PS5 base console, it is not powerful enough to run the game’s complex simulation at higher frame rates."

Head of development Rob Nelson framed the decision to skip performance mode in much simpler terms to IGN:

"It wouldn’t have been acceptable to anybody. The simple answer is, when you ask the technical team, they’re, like, ‘Have you seen it?’ There’s too many compromises that would’ve had to have been made to do that, is the short answer," he said. "Too much, too much."

Keep up to date with the most important stories and the best deals, as picked by the PC Gamer team.

While I don't actually have a problem playing a slow-paced game like GTA 6 at half the usual framerate so long as it's consistent and smooth, I can't deny that these quotes left me cracking a smile in the direction of my PC.

The world of Leonida does look unbelievably impressive at times—both in terms of pure graphical oomph and the density of vehicles, NPCs, and reactive foliage—but a great PC is going to demolish it. I've been searching for a game that will make this RTX 5090 actually flinch, and honestly, I'm doubtful even GTA 6 will be it. Barring a suite of PC-only enhancements that raise its requirements by a lot, I can't imagine a game that targets an Xbox Series S will have trouble blowing past 60 fps on top PC hardware.

This is putting into perspective for me that, while I wasn't looking, the current consoles got old. That's fine, to be clear—we're in the middle of a tech pause that has me happily playing older games anyway—but it's a wasted opportunity that GTA 6 is debuting exclusively on mid hardware.

We have to wait an unspecified amount of time to get what is destined to be the best version of this generational game. As Chris said in his writeup after 100 hours with GTA 6, "It's (mostly) great. But it will be (mostly) so much greater when it comes to PC."

#3902. Ubisoft is reportedly making a new Rainbow Six Vegas game, nearly two decades after Vegas 2

Ubisoft is reportedly working on a new Rainbow Six Vegas game 18 years after the last entry in the series.

According to Insider Gaming, the project is in early development at Ubisoft Montreal under the codename Spades. It’s one of three new projects reportedly in production at the studio, and sources suggest a second of those is also set in the Rainbow Six universe. Eurogamer hasn’t been able to verify the report.

It’s not yet clear what form the new game will take, but Insider Gaming’s sources said it's "likely Vegas 3 rather than a remake" of an existing game. Insider Gaming expects it will be several years before Ubisoft officially announces a new Vegas game.

Rainbow Six Vegas launched in 2006, followed by Rainbow Six Vegas 2 in 2008. Since then, the series has centred on 2015's Rainbow Six Siege, and in August, Ubisoft announced Rainbow Six Tactics, a single-player, turn-based spin-off from Ubisoft Paris due in 2027.

Rainbow Six now sits under Vantage Studios, the Ubisoft subsidiary set up last year that also oversees Assassin’s Creed and Far Cry, and in which Tencent holds a 26.32 percent stake.

Last week, we learned that Ubisoft is reportedly working on two new Assassin's Creed games: one set in ancient Rome, and a mobile spin-off set in Jerusalem. The leak came less than a week after Ubisoft issued a statement about the future of the Assassin's Creed series, insisting there are currently no new remakes of the series' past games in the works.

The next set of Pokemon cards has been unveiled, and it promises to be a heavy hitter - literally.

In terms of what else we can expect from the expansion, it'll span the usual booster packs, an Elite Trainer Box, and "various collections" according to the press release.

We don't know what all those cards will be just yet, but if prerelease starts in January, it probably won't be long before we find out.

#3898. The latest GTA 6 leak comes in the form of a 34-song tracklist for GTA 6: The Album, featuring Dua Lipa, Lana Del Rey, Rina Sawayama, and more

We are now just four days away from the release of GTA 6 on Xbox Series X/S and PS5, but the proximity to the much-anticipated launch date isn't stemming the tide of leaks that has been plaguing the game for much of the past year. Yesterday, a new video - seemingly from a record store that received vinyl records of the soundtrack early - showed off the full 34-song tracklist for the game.

Thanks to the listing printed on the back of Grand Theft Auto 6: The Album vinyl, we have a better idea of the licensed music that'll appear in-game. Travis Scott, Rina Sawayama, Cardi B, Pinkpantheress, SZA, Keith Richards, Dua Lipa, Jennie, Lana Del Rey, Zara Larsson are just some of the names that make up the impressive list. We know about a few of these tracks from September's announcement of the record, but only six tracks were revealed then, not the whole list.

Take a look at the full track listing below:

You can expect to hear these tracks on the radio - alongside many more, no doubt - and deployed at curated times during cutscenes or in missions, to really tie together the vibe of the city. This is something Vice City did remarkably well its roster of 80s tracks, and I can't wait to see how Rockstar has used more contemporary music in the same way here.

Of course, there have been a lot of Grand Theft Auto 6 leaks in the run-up to the game's launch. Another recent example is the full game's map which seemingly leaked online thanks to the £350 collector's edition on show in a UK department store. Then there were all the leaks from a group calling itself CyberLeek, which shared unofficial gameplay and map details over the course of a few weeks, before Rockstar had even revealed much gameplay itself.

Amongst all this, Rockstar has been embroiled in legal action after it was accused of union busting following the firing of over 30 employees. The case's conclusion will be determined this week, as the game goes on sale.

#3897. Homura Hime coming to PS5 in 2027

Publisher PLAYISM and developer Crimson Dusk will release 3D bullet hell action game Homura Hime for PlayStation 5 in 2027, the companies announced. It will launch alongside its previously announced Switch 2 version, which was originally planned for 2026.

Homura Hime first launched for PC via Steam on March 4.

Here is an overview of the game, via PLAYISM:

Homura Hime is a third-person bullet hell action game that combines fast-paced, combo-oriented combat with dazzling Japanese anime-style visuals. With a vibrant aesthetic that aims to recreate the richness and dynamism of hand-drawn Japanese animation, Homura Hime tasks players with ridding the world of the fiendish Archdemon Girls and their monster hordes, utilizing slick melee combat evocative of the NieR and Devil May Cry series. Dodge the barrages of enemy attacks and string together flashy combos to clear the battlefield, excising tainted souls from a troubled world and unraveling the mysterious legacy of the titular heroine.

Welcome to a world populated by both humans and demons. Here, troubled souls burdened by intense emotion or deep regret are transformed into archdemons when they pass through the veil of mortality. These archdemons have the power to corrupt the very foundation of the world, contaminating their surroundings and the creatures who dwell within them. Those tainted by this demonic power turn into lowly monsters; vicious fiends that operate solely on raw instinct. When this world becomes threatened by a quintet of extremely powerful Archdemon Girls, the High Priestess has no other choice but to turn to Homura Hime, the “Flame Princess” and the strongest exorcist. Alongside her devoted aide Ann, Homura Hime must embark on a divine mission to eliminate the five Archdemon Girls and their monster hordes, banishing their evil and purifying her discordant world.

While most game studios are carefully avoiding the Grand Theft Auto 6 behemoth, Devolver Digital has relentlessly and theatrically pursued it. In May 2025 it pledged to launch a game on May 26, head-to-head with GTA 6—and when GTA 6 was delayed, Devolver delayed too.

And now, with GTA 6 slowly rolling through its official launch on November 19, it's finally (almost) here: Volvy's Adventure: Reslimed, "a spectacular remaster of the original remake of the unreleased action-platformer starring the most famous videogame mascot of all time," developed by Gunbrella/Gato Roboto studio Doinksoft.

So, first things first: As the word "unreleased" amidst that slurry of words from the Steam page suggests, this is not actually a remake of a popular game from the days of yore, although it certainly has the vibe, and actually looks pretty decent as these things go. And yes, Volvy is indeed Devolver's mascot—here's some massively overpriced merchandise, if you're into that, or just want evidence.

"Adventure across four revamped worlds full of naughty baddies and menacing boss fights while collecting delicious onions to keep Volvy at extreme levels of awesome," Devolver said of the game. "There's some sort of story too. Basically some warlocks released some slime and Volvy is stopping them. Also, they kidnapped his friends."

What really brings us here, though, is that dogged pursuit of GTA 6. It's obviously coattails marketing, but as PC Gamer's Shaun Prescott said in 2025, it's a pretty good bit—and Devolver is really sticking with it.

Yes indeed, the Volvy's Adventure: Reslimed launch trailer is a virtual shot-for-shot remake of the GTA 6 launch trailer, music and all.
